items.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025
items.q: You know Eddie Bert had a fantastic story.

ctx.x: I figured out that it was possible, and that’s what I wanted to do. So I had this day job at NBC, which my mom would help me get, and I was happy working there. And you know if you join NBC at a lesser capacity, like the mail room or the parking lot, you essentially would be in the organization and then they — when they found a place they’d maybe move you up to something more, you know better in the business. And my dad had worked for NBC for years so you know I got hired because the president of NBC told them to…
You know Eddie Bert had a fantastic story.

I thought I’d be able to make it, I think I’m going to be okay. By that time I was 19, was already getting calls to play with a lot of people, was playing with really bass players like Red, and Gary Peacock was a friend and he really liked my playing ‘cause I was more adventurous than the people he played with. And he was, you know what happened to him?
